source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey, good work on the board! I went through the schematic and PCB files in detail, overall it looks solid. Just a few things I noticed, can you take a look and tell me what you think:

1\. USB-C connector (USB1) — DRC is showing hole clearance violations and negative annular width on the 2 mounting pin holes. Looks like the footprint has the drill larger than the copper pad. Will JLCPCB accept this
or does it need fixing?
2\. VMID (pin 36) on AXP2101 — in the PCB it's connected to the same net as VSYS. VMID is supposed to be the internal ADC reference, I would expect it to just have a cap to GND and be isolated from VSYS. Can you
double check this against the datasheet or a reference design?
3\. R6 (4.7k) — D1 LED is marked DNP which makes sense, but R6 which is the current limiting resistor for it is still in the BOM and will be assembled. Since D1 isn't placed, R6 will have a floating pin. Should R6
also be DNP, or is there a reason to keep it?
4\. VSIS net name — I think this is a typo for VSYS, just cosmetic but worth fixing to avoid confusion.
5\. L1 inductor footprint — DRC is flagging that L\_Changjiang\_FTC404020S is not found in the standard KiCad library, it's using a local override. Just want to confirm the footprint physically matches the 4.7uH
inductor you're planning to use.

execution.observed_behavior: KiCad DRC reports that the L1 inductor footprint is unavailable in the standard library and relies on a local override.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: The footprint for the 4.7uH is in the standard KiCad Inductor\_SMD library

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports that the 4.7uH inductor footprint is available in KiCad's standard Inductor_SMD library.
After checking the specified standard-library path, the client still cannot locate the inductor footprint.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: It works, the warning is gone now.

execution.observed_behavior: The client confirms that the inductor footprint now resolves and the KiCad warning is gone.

Q\_SOT-23.step (from the JLCPCB plugin library) — for Q3
TS-1088-AR02016.step (from the JLCPCB plugin library) — for S1

Once I have them I'll drop them into the project's libs/easyeda/easyeda.3dshapes/ folder. Thanks!

source_message.text: Yeah, Also ${KICAD8\_3RD\_PARTY} is a KiCad 8 path variable — KiCad 9 uses ${KICAD9\_3RD\_PARTY} — so even on a machine where the JLCPCB plugin is installed, those refs would break in KiCad 9.

value_updates.kicad_library_variable_compatibility: Library references must remain compatible with KiCad 9 rather than relying on the KiCad 8-only ${KICAD8_3RD_PARTY} variable.
